messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: ACME TCO + next steps

Hi Sophie / Jordan — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap of what we heard, our topline TCO levers, and next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of pain points / goals
- High per-month spend driven by a mix of long prompts (avg turn length ~1.8k tokens) and many small, interactive calls (~120k calls/month).
- Latency-sensitive flows (customer-facing chat) require ~200–300ms p95.
- Budget: you mentioned an internal target of ~$150k/year for inference (pilot -> scale).
- Primary goal: cut unit token cost while keeping reply quality and latency.

Suggested cost/TCO levers we discussed
1) Model + quantization tradeoffs — moving from a 13B float model to a 7B-quantized variant (rwd-7b-q4) reduces per-token inference compute by ~2.5–3x with ~small quality delta for your retrieval-augmented prompts.
2) Batching & dynamic batching — batching similar short-turn requests together can reduce GPU utilization by ~25–40% on interactive workloads. We’ll demo request coalescing and target batch sizes tuned to your latency SLO.
3) Prefix / KV caching — for repeated system prompts and common prefixes, KV caching can reduce token generation by ~30–50% on your FAQ/chat flows.
4) Routing to cheaper variants — route non-latency critical tasks (analytics, nightly re-ranking) to lower-cost models or background pipelines.
5) Autoscaling + reserved capacity — 1) reserved Dedicated pool for predictable throughput and 2) burst to hosted for spikes to avoid overprovisioning.

Ballpark economics (very rough, for discussion)
- Current observed usage (your numbers): ~1.5B tokens/month.
- Baseline hosted float model cost (example): $1.60 / 1M tokens => ~$2,400/month.
- With rwd-7b-q4 + batching + caching conservative estimate: 3x compute reduction + 35% token reduction => effective cost reduction ~75% => ~$600/month.
- If you require enterprise SLA and Dedicated capacity, blended cost will be higher; we’ll show a committed pricing scenario vs on-demand.

Attachments: I’ve attached a TCO worksheet (redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx) with line-item assumptions so your finance team can tweak inputs. Also included a short product sheet.

Proposed next steps
- I’ll send a short, one-page monthly estimate for the three scenarios (pilot hosted, committed Dedicated 12mo, and hybrid). (Action: Ben — by Mon 6/7)
- Technical demo of batching & KV caching with your prompt set (30–45m). (Action: Marissa to run demo — target week of 6/14)
- Shared MUTUAL ACTION PLAN: finalize SOW/procurement timeline; Sophie to confirm procurement window and any required compliance items (SOC 2, DPA).

Please reply with any corrections to assumptions and confirm the best time for the demo.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
